body.statement: Suppose a legal realization has strictly positive \(\alpha\) and \(P\), interior hazards and emissions, and two states \(i,j\) with identical emission profiles. If \(h_i\ne h_j\) and \((Pe)_i\ne(Pe)_j\), then a relatively open neighborhood within the aliased model contains a continuum of legal non-permutation realizations with the same complete observed stopped-panel law and different \(\mu^0_{g,1}\) for every supported cohort \(g\). Along the alias-preserving direction, the derivative is \((\alpha K_0^g)_i(h_j-h_i)((Pe)_j-(Pe)_i)/\{(1-h_i)p_g\}\).
body.justification: The converse diagnoses attempts to transport a weighted-HMM or latent-Markov parametric g-formula workflow to stopped panels while requiring continuation to be determined by the observed stopped law.
body.gap: Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci and Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt impose their own propensity, exchangeability, measurement, and structural-model conditions. This theorem does not contradict those procedures; it shows that without an additional restriction, unequal within-alias hazards and forecasts prevent a unique observed-stopped-law continuation.
body.consumer: A transported fitted-latent-state workflow receives a precise warning: on an alias block, observed-stopped-law-determined continuation requires an extra restriction unless the forecast contrast is degenerate.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(e_k\) denote the \(k\)-th coordinate column, and set
\[
 A=e_i(e_j-e_i)^{\top},\qquad S(t)=I_K+tA.
\]
Then \(A\mathbf 1_K=0\), so \(S(t)\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_K\).  Because states \(i\) and \(j\) have identical emission profiles, \(A B_a=B_a A\) for every \(a\in\mathcal Y\), and hence \(S(t)B_a=B_aS(t)\).  For all sufficiently small \(|t|\), \(S(t)\) is invertible.  Define
\[
 \alpha(t)=\alpha S(t),\quad h(t)=S(t)^{-1}h,
 \quad K_0(t)=S(t)^{-1}K_0S(t),
 \quad P(t)=\{I_K-\operatorname{diag}(h(t))\}^{-1}K_0(t),       \tag{14}
\]
and leave every \(B_a\) unchanged.  At \(t=0\), all entries of \(\alpha\) and \(P\), all hazards, and all emission probabilities are strictly positive.  These inequalities are open.  Hazard overlap also makes the diagonal inverse in (14) continuous near zero.  Therefore, after reducing the neighborhood of zero if necessary, \(\alpha(t)\) is a positive probability row, \(h(t)\) is interior, and \(P(t)\) is entrywise positive.

To check stochasticity rather than assume it, use \(K_0\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_K-h\) and \(S(t)\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_K\):
\[
 K_0(t)\mathbf 1_K
 =S(t)^{-1}K_0\mathbf 1_K
 =\mathbf 1_K-h(t).
\]
Thus \(P(t)\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_K\).  Also \(\alpha(t)\mathbf 1_K=1\).  Hence (14) is a continuum of legal stochastic realizations.  Invertibility of \(K_0(t)\) and predictive rank are preserved by similarity.

Writing \(M_a(t)=B_aK_0(t)\), commutation gives
\[
 M_a(t)=S(t)^{-1}M_aS(t),
 \qquad
 M_w(t)=S(t)^{-1}M_wS(t).                                    \tag{15}
\]
Therefore, for every word \(w\),
\[
 \alpha(t)M_w(t)\mathbf 1_K=\alpha M_w\mathbf 1_K,
 \qquad
 \alpha(t)M_w(t)h(t)=\alpha M_wh.                            \tag{16}
\]
Thus the complete risk- and adoption-terminal stopped law is constant along the path.  The same conditional law of realized post-adoption outcomes can be attached to every member, so the complete observed-panel law is also constant.  Since \(h_i\ne h_j\), the path is nonconstant and, except at isolated parameter values, is not a latent permutation.  Every sufficiently small relative neighborhood in the fixed alias stratum consequently contains a continuum of these legal realizations.

It remains to show that the causal continuation changes.  Express the varying hazard in the original coordinate system as
\[
 J(t)=S(t)\operatorname{diag}(h(t))S(t)^{-1}.
\]
Since \(S'(0)=A\) and \(h'(0)=-Ah\), differentiation gives
\[
 \dot J(0)=[A,D]-\operatorname{diag}(Ah)
 =(h_j-h_i)e_i(e_j-e_i)^{\top},
 \qquad \dot J(0)\mathbf 1_K=0.                              \tag{17}
\]
In these fixed coordinates the de-killed transition associated with \(J\) is \(P_J=(I_K-J)^{-1}K_0\).  Thus
\[
 \dot P_J(0)=(I_K-D)^{-1}\dot J(0)P.                         \tag{18}
\]
The denominator \(p_g=\alpha K_0^gh\) is fixed along the same-observed-law path.  Differentiating the one-step causal numerator and using \(I_K+D(I_K-D)^{-1}=(I_K-D)^{-1}\), equations (17)--(18) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left.\frac{d}{dt}\mu^0_{g,1}(t)\right|_{t=0}
 &=\frac{\alpha K_0^g\{\dot J(0)Pe+D(I_K-D)^{-1}\dot J(0)Pe\}}{p_g}\\
 &=\frac{(\alpha K_0^g)_i(h_j-h_i)\{(Pe)_j-(Pe)_i\}}{(1-h_i)p_g}. \tag{19}
\end{aligned}
\]
All denominators in (19) are positive: \(1-h_i>0\) by overlap and \(p_g>0\) for a supported cohort.  Moreover, strict positivity of \(\alpha\), \(P\), and \(1-h\) makes every entry of \(\alpha K_0^g\) positive.  The two stated contrasts are nonzero, so (19) is nonzero for every supported \(g\).  Continuity then supplies arbitrarily close path points with different \(\mu^0_{g,1}\).  Keeping the treated-outcome law fixed makes the corresponding ATT values differ with the opposite sign, completing the converse.
